advice: Abstain. The supplied source and compiler output show that `sme_transpose` materializes all of `at` before `sme_gemm` consumes it. A proposal that feeds a small transposed A tile directly to MOPA would need to change the loop order or retain partial C across more reduction work. The supplied evidence does not establish a new legal design that avoids the known partial-C spill/reload cost. No complete source or compiler output for a distinct tile-fusion design is supplied, so I cannot verify that it is absent from the current code or avoid repeating the rejected tradeoff. The fresh baseline is 1372.78–1504.19 GFLOP/s; it provides no evidence for a fusion change.
risks: Any fused design must count repeated transpose work and all scratch traffic inside the timed `gemm` call. It must preserve FP32 MOPA selectors 0–3, increasing-k arithmetic, general-size and odd-tail behavior, and tolerance 0.002. No performance claim is supported without compiler output and fresh paired AC measurements.
